output.title: Sign in to SoFa with development Keycloak in Aspire and connect GitHub
output.problem: The personal factory owner needs an authenticated local operational workspace and a separately authorized GitHub acting identity before production identity infrastructure exists. The current observer is unauthenticated and read-only; the Aspire host composes no application resources. Add a bounded application security foundation without putting SoFa in repository execution or approval paths.
actors: Juan García Carmona, personal factory owner and solo developer
Developers exercising the local workspace on desktop and phone over trusted LAN/VPN
scope: Compose a dedicated development Keycloak and the SoFa application in the existing Aspire solution, with pinned integration and reproducible test realm/client settings.
Define one application authentication boundary supporting development issuer configuration and an externally configured production issuer without provisioning production infrastructure.
Authorize the configured owner by stable provider identity; keep application sessions and provider/GitHub credentials server-side.
Link a GitHub user through explicit separate authorization, display the acting identity, and evaluate configured repository permissions server-side.
Preserve repository-owned workflow authority and source identities. Authentication does not authorize workflow dispatch, implementation, approval or merge.
outOfScope: Production Keycloak installation or production readiness certification
Household onboarding, multi-user administration, tenancy and backup destination selection
New workflow controls, an execution queue, supervisor revival or an alternate lifecycle policy engine
Implementation, proposal approval, deployment and merge in this run

acceptanceCriteria.condition: Starting the existing Aspire solution composes the application and a dedicated development Keycloak with pinned versions, test realm/client configuration and stable browser-reachable endpoints; it starts neither a production provider connection nor the retired supervisor.

The same application boundary supports an externally configured production issuer on [production host] without provisioning that provider; development accounts, callbacks and credentials remain distinct from production.

Unauthenticated requests cannot read protected workspace data or perform writes; only the configured stable provider identity is admitted. Evidence demonstrates successful login/logout, session expiry, non-owner denial, forged callback rejection and CSRF rejection using server-side session protection.

GitHub linking requires a separate explicit user authorization, displays the verified acting account and checks configured repository permissions on the server. An unlinked or insufficiently permitted account is not represented as authorized, and no installation bot impersonates the user.
Provider and GitHub tokens are absent from browser storage, logs and retained evidence; development does not reuse production credentials.

The adopted Lighthouse package version and applicable delivered OIDC guidance are identified and reused without a local policy fork. Actual provider login and source identity are demonstrated separately from documentation compliance.

The full development login and GitHub-linking flow is exercised on desktop and a phone over LAN/VPN against a designated real test repository. The implementation proposal states session assurance and timeout values explicitly.

affectedBehaviour: src/web/server.mjs currently serves GET/HEAD assets and observations without application login, rejects writes and uses server-side observation collection. The proposal must identify the protected workspace boundary and explain whether the existing read-only LAN view remains separate or becomes protected; it must not accidentally add unauthenticated mutation routes.
src/SoFa.AppHost/AppHost.cs currently builds an empty distributed application; adding composition must preserve its prohibition on supervisor and execution-database startup.

README.md describes operator gh authentication for observation. The proposal must distinguish this existing credential source from the separately authorized GitHub user connection and prevent account confusion.
constraints: Use maintained OIDC middleware and an external provider; no bespoke password store or authorization server.
BR-LAN-PRIVILEGE-BOUNDARY requires a separately accepted security boundary before privileged controls; no exception is recorded.
ADR-0006 remains accepted. Proposed decisions and issue text do not supersede it.
Product semantics change through a human-approved Product Change; refinement neither applies nor accepts that change.
No external services, credentials or live runtime were accessed during refinement.

qualityExpectations.security: Fail closed for unauthenticated, non-owner and insufficient-repository-permission cases; use stable issuer/subject identity, server-side sessions and token custody, callback/CSRF protections and environment isolation.
qualityExpectations.mobile: Owner login and identity linking must remain usable on desktop and a real phone with browser-reachable LAN/VPN endpoints.
qualityExpectations.accessibility: Preserve usable login, denial and identity-status interactions across desktop/mobile; detailed accessibility test coverage belongs in the proposal.
qualityExpectations.performance: No new numeric latency target is supplied; preserve existing observer behavior and record any session or identity-provider availability impact in the proposal.
